name: US–China / Taiwan
summary: Taiwan tracked 2 Chinese military aircraft and 7 ships on 20–21 Nov, after a 100+ vessel deployment in early November
state: Taiwan's defence ministry tracked two Chinese military aircraft, six naval vessels and one official ship around the island in the 24 hours to 06:00 on 21 Nov, with both aircraft crossing the median line (Taiwan News). In early November Taiwan reported more than 100 Chinese naval and coastguard vessels across the western Pacific and a one-day high of 49 aircraft sorties (SCMP). No blockade or clash was found, so Watch holds.
for_you: Tensions are elevated but routine trade and travel continue. Firms reliant on Taiwan-made chips and Taiwan Strait shipping are the most exposed to any escalation.
rubric_hit: Large-scale PLA deployments around Taiwan = Watch

sources.title: Taiwan News — Taiwan tracks 2 Chinese military aircraft, 7 ships and 4 balloons
SCMP — Taiwan flags massive PLA naval mobilisation, spike in air sorties

why: The world's two largest economies; a Taiwan crisis would halt most advanced chip supply and risk great-power war.
drivers: PLA exercises, tariffs and tech controls, diplomacy, Taiwan politics, South China Sea incidents.

rubric.alert: Blockade or 'quarantine' of Taiwan, military clash, or severed diplomatic channels.
rubric.watch: Large-scale PLA exercises around Taiwan, major new sanctions/controls, or a naval/air incident.
rubric.normal: Managed relations; dialogue channels open; routine PLA activity.
